doc.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022

title: Learning arranging by ear and from Fania recordings
summary: Never studied arranging formally; learned from hearing Fania recordings, asking pianists for licks; Fania required arrangers in the studio unpaid for conducting.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Well you know I never studied arranging formally. I studied, I was a trumpet player and the trumpet teachers that I had were very proud of the fact that I became a very good sight reader and I was able to play with good technique. But as far as arranging was concerned, that was a matter of my good luck and being involved with some very good musicians, and also using my ear to determine what kind of things I wanted to write. Plus I was very lucky in the early stages. I was doing a lot of writing for a company called Fania Records, which was like the Latin Motown. And the vast majority of those arrangements were being recorded and as a result I can listen to the recordings and I learned certain things did not sound as good as I thought that they were going to, and there were others that sounded a little better than I thought they were going to. And in between those things and also whenever I was at a — either at a gig or a recording session, everyone warms up and when the piano player would warm up and I would hear him play something that I really liked but that I wasn’t able to duplicate, I would go over to him and ask him, “What was that that you just played?” and get a piece of paper and write out five lines real quick and take it home and work on it and work on it so that became part of my vocabulary as well.
Oh, that’s a great story. Were you usually in the studio when bands were playing your charts?
Yes. With Fania in particular, they wanted the arrangers to be there to quote make sure your arrangements sounded good and by the way, not pay you for even being in the studio to conduct.
They’d pay for the arrangement but not for the conducting. But that was their policy.
Yeah, like it’s not our fault if something doesn’t sound quite the way —
